Testing a true one-rep max at 16 isn't off-limits, but I'd hold off on it for now. Your skeleton and technique are still developing, and a heavy single gives you very little that a good set of 3 to 5 reps doesn't. Most coaches who work with teens, and the youth strength guidelines, favor building a solid base first: clean technique, controlled reps, and loads you can move well.

If you want to know where your strength stands, work up to a hard set of 3 to 5 with good form and I can estimate your max from it. That's safer and tells you nearly the same thing. If you do ever test a true max, do it with a spotter or on safeties, after a proper warm-up, and with someone who knows lifting watching your form.

It's also worth asking your doctor or a qualified coach in person whether anything about your own situation changes that. Want me to pull your recent numbers and see where your estimated maxes sit?
